title: Naseeruddin Shah Breaks Down Over Police Crackdown on Students, Compares Delhi Police to ICE Agents
excerpt: The veteran actor condemned the use of force during the CJP-led 'Chalo Sansad' march in Delhi, while a separate viral video falsely claiming he attended the Jantar Mantar protest was debunked as old footage from Mumbai.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Naseeruddin Shah condemned police violence against student protesters in an emotional video.
  • He compared Delhi Police to ICE agents, criticizing their brutality.
  • A viral video claiming Shah attended a protest was debunked as old footage.
  • Shah joins numerous celebrities supporting the student movement for accountability.
  • The movement follows a Supreme Court judge's derogatory remarks about unemployed youth.
https://www.instagram.com/p/DbGQ57yGspQ/

An Actor's Anguish

Naseeruddin Shah, one of Indian cinema's most respected voices, released a video through the Cockroach Janta Party's official X handle on Tuesday in which he broke down while condemning the police violence against students during the previous day's march on Parliament.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=FxuAP1rOcew

Speaking in Hindi, the 76-year-old actor did not mince words. He compared Delhi Police officers — faces covered, batons in hand — to agents of the United States' Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), a force that has faced widespread allegations of brutality.

"My heart is full and I am boiling with anger seeing the kind of cruelty being inflicted on our children by those thugs who remind me of America's ICE agents — faces masked, batons in hand. Think of your own children sometime."

— Naseeruddin Shah, via CJP's X handle

Shah expressed solidarity with the protesters, adding: "Many people's sympathies are with you. Many people are with you. Keep fighting. I have always had hope in our country's youth, and now that hope shines brighter."

> **"Delhi Police said nearly 180 people were injured, including 118 security personnel and 60 protesters."**

"Delhi Police said nearly 180 people were injured, including 118 security personnel and 60 protesters."

What Triggered the Violence

Shah's remarks followed violent clashes that erupted on Monday when thousands of CJP supporters attempted to march from Jantar Mantar to Parliament during the opening day of the monsoon session. Delhi Police deployed multi-layered barricades, heavy personnel, and imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

https://x.com/TheQuint/status/2079530264955597124

When protesters tried to push past the barricades, police responded with baton charges and tear gas, according to Reuters. Delhi Police said nearly 180 people were injured, including 118 security personnel and 60 protesters. The CJP said more than 150 protesters required hospital treatment.

On Tuesday, more than 5,000 protesters returned to Jantar Mantar, though the CJP said it would not attempt another march on Parliament to avoid further violence. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and his sister Priyanka Vadra were detained outside PM Modi's residence after protesting the crackdown, according to ANI.

Viral Video Debunked

Separately, a video began circulating on social media claiming to show Naseeruddin Shah at the Jantar Mantar protest site. Fact-checkers from multiple outlets, including iDiva and Zoom TV, established that the footage was shot outside Mumbai's Regal Cinema in Colaba and was originally posted by Instagram user Rajesh Gaur on July 15 — days before Monday's march.

Shah has not publicly addressed the misidentification, though the timeline makes the claim impossible. What is confirmed is that Shah and his wife Ratna Pathak Shah signed a joint statement — alongside writer Arundhati Roy, economist Jayati Ghosh, and other public figures — supporting activist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike since June 28.

Bollywood Splits on the Movement

The CJP-led student movement has drawn an unusual breadth of celebrity support. Hrithik Roshan, Arijit Singh, Dia Mirza, Sonakshi Sinha, Zeenat Aman, Diljit Dosanjh, Prakash Raj, and Shabana Azmi have all voiced solidarity with the protesters. Azmi and Raj have physically attended events.

On the other side, BJP MPs Kangana Ranaut and Hema Malini have publicly opposed the protests, calling them disruptive.

The movement began after the Supreme Court's Chief Justice reportedly compared some unemployed young Indians to "cockroaches" during an unrelated hearing. Supporters embraced the insult, turning it into the satirical Cockroach Janta Party, which has attracted millions of followers demanding accountability for the NEET exam paper leak in May that affected 2 million students.

What Comes Next

Prime Minister Modi's first comments on the crisis came Tuesday, relayed through Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju: the government acted immediately on exam irregularities, 13 people have been arrested, and a re-examination was successfully conducted. Health Minister J.P. Nadda has agreed to meet CJP representatives to discuss their demands.

The Delhi High Court on Tuesday allowed Sonam Wangchuk to be shifted from government custody to a private hospital — fulfilling one of three CJP demands. The remaining two — Pradhan's resignation and compensation for students who died by suicide — appear far from resolution.
